project.title: Who Controlled India And How Did People Respond?
project.subtitle: A political history of the Indian subcontinent

control.name: Indus urban societies
control.description: Large urban settlements develop across the Indus River system. Their exact political structure remains uncertain.

response.title: Organized urban life
response.description: People participate in highly organized cities, craft production and long-distance trade networks.

change.title: Urban civilization emerges
change.description: Large planned settlements appear across a broad region of the northwestern subcontinent.

eras.title: Indus Cities Decline
eras.subtitle: A transformation, not a sudden disappearance

control.name: Regional communities
control.description: The large urban system of the Indus Valley changes significantly, with many major cities declining.

response.title: Communities reorganize
response.description: Population and settlement patterns shift toward smaller and more regional communities.

change.title: The urban network fragments
change.description: The political and economic landscape becomes more decentralized.

control.name: Tribal and early kingdoms
control.description: Political communities develop across northern India, with authority often organized around chiefs and emerging kings.

response.title: New social and political structures
response.description: Communities adapt to changing settlement patterns and increasingly complex political organizations.

change.title: Political organization evolves
change.description: Power gradually becomes more structured as communities expand eastward.

control.name: Multiple kingdoms and republics
control.description: Sixteen major political powers emerge across northern India, including Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa and Avanti.

response.title: Cities and trade expand
response.description: Merchants, farmers and urban communities become increasingly connected to competing states.

change.title: India becomes politically competitive
change.description: Power is divided among numerous kingdoms and republics rather than one dominant empire.

control.name: Kingdom of Magadha
control.description: Magadha grows into the most powerful state in northern India through military expansion, diplomacy and control of strategic resources.

response.title: Diplomacy and incorporation
response.description: Neighboring states interact with Magadha through warfare, alliances and political accommodation.

change.title: Power concentrates in eastern India
change.description: Magadha becomes the foundation for later imperial expansion.

eras.title: Buddhism Emerges
eras.subtitle: A new religious and political influence

control.name: Regional kingdoms and republics
control.description: Buddhism develops within a politically competitive landscape dominated by states such as Magadha and Kosala.

response.title: New ideas challenge established traditions
response.description: Buddhist communities develop outside traditional political and religious structures.

change.title: Religion becomes politically influential
change.description: New religious communities eventually become important partners and critics of rulers.

control.name: Mauryan Empire
control.description: Chandragupta Maurya establishes an empire centered on Magadha and expands across much of northern India.

response.title: Regional powers are incorporated
response.description: Local territories are brought into a centralized imperial administration through conquest, diplomacy and governance.

change.title: Imperial rule expands dramatically
change.description: Political authority becomes concentrated under a single imperial government across a large part of the subcontinent.

control.name: Mauryan Empire
control.description: Ashoka becomes emperor of one of the largest states in the ancient Indian subcontinent.

response.title: A new model of imperial rule
response.description: Ashoka increasingly emphasizes dhamma, moral conduct and welfare alongside imperial administration.

change.title: Imperial ideology changes
change.description: Ashoka uses inscriptions and public works to communicate a new vision of kingship.

control.name: Mauryan Empire
control.description: Ashoka's forces conquer Kalinga after a major and destructive war.

response.title: Kalinga resists conquest
response.description: Kalinga's resistance becomes a defining moment in Ashoka's reign.

change.title: A turning point for Ashoka
change.description: The war is followed by Ashoka's increasing emphasis on dhamma and opposition to unnecessary violence.

control.name: Regional successor states
control.description: The Mauryan Empire collapses after the assassination of its last ruler, Brihadratha.

response.title: Regional powers return
response.description: Political authority becomes increasingly decentralized as new dynasties emerge.

change.title: Imperial unity breaks apart
change.description: The subcontinent returns to a landscape dominated by multiple regional powers.

control.name: Multiple regional dynasties
control.description: Indo-Greek, Shaka, Satavahana, Kushan and other powers control different parts of the subcontinent.

response.title: Regional identities strengthen
response.description: Communities adapt to changing rulers while trade and cultural exchange connect distant regions.

change.title: No single empire dominates
change.description: Political authority becomes distributed among numerous regional powers.

control.name: Gupta Empire
control.description: The Gupta dynasty establishes a powerful state in northern India.

response.title: Regional integration
response.description: Local rulers and communities operate within a political system combining direct rule, alliances and subordinate kingdoms.

change.title: Northern India reunifies under imperial power
change.description: The Guptas establish one of the major political powers of early classical India.

control.name: Kingdom of Harsha
control.description: Harsha establishes a large kingdom across much of northern India.

response.title: Regional cooperation and rivalry
response.description: Harsha's authority depends on relationships with regional rulers rather than complete centralized control.

change.title: Northern India briefly reconsolidates
change.description: A major political center emerges after the decline of Gupta power.

control.name: Regional dynasties
control.description: Pratiharas, Rashtrakutas, Palas, Cholas and many other dynasties compete for political power.

response.title: Regional societies flourish
response.description: Local rulers, religious institutions, merchants and communities develop distinctive political and cultural systems.

change.title: Political power becomes highly regional
change.description: No single empire controls most of the subcontinent for an extended period.

control.name: Chola Empire
control.description: The Cholas expand across southern India and project power across the Indian Ocean.

response.title: Local administration and trade
response.description: Village institutions, temples and merchant networks become important parts of Chola political life.

change.title: Southern India becomes an imperial center
change.description: The Cholas demonstrate that major imperial power can emerge outside northern India.

eras.title: Second Battle of Tarain
eras.subtitle: A major shift in North Indian power

control.name: Ghurid forces
control.description: Muhammad Ghori defeats Prithviraja III, opening the way for Ghurid expansion in northern India.

response.title: Rajput resistance
response.description: Regional Rajput powers resist the expansion of Ghurid authority.

change.title: Delhi becomes a center of expanding Islamic rule
change.description: The victory helps establish the political foundations for the Delhi Sultanate.

control.name: Delhi Sultanate
control.description: Qutb ud-Din Aibak establishes an independent sultanate centered on Delhi.

response.title: Regional resistance and accommodation
response.description: Rajput states and other regional powers resist expansion while some local rulers negotiate with the Sultanate.

change.title: A new political center emerges
change.description: Delhi becomes the center of a succession of powerful dynasties ruling large parts of northern India.

control.name: Delhi Sultanate
control.description: Alauddin Khalji greatly expands the Sultanate's influence and launches campaigns into the Deccan.

response.title: Regional kingdoms resist
response.description: Rajput and Deccan powers resist military expansion while some accept tributary relationships.

change.title: Northern power reaches deeper into the Deccan
change.description: The political balance of the subcontinent shifts as Delhi projects power farther south.

control.name: Vijayanagara Empire
control.leader: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I
control.description: The Vijayanagara Empire emerges in southern India and becomes a major counterweight to northern and Deccan powers.

response.title: Southern political resistance
response.description: Vijayanagara becomes a major center of resistance and regional consolidation.

change.title: Power shifts toward the south
change.description: Southern India develops a powerful state capable of competing with neighboring sultanates.

control.name: Mughal Empire
control.description: Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi and establishes Mughal control over Delhi and Agra.

response.title: Regional resistance and alliances
response.description: Regional powers resist Mughal expansion while others negotiate or form alliances with the new empire.

change.title: A new imperial dynasty takes power
change.description: The Lodi dynasty falls and Mughal rule begins in northern India.

control.name: Sur Empire
control.description: Sher Shah defeats Humayun and establishes the Sur Empire.

response.title: Administrative reform
response.description: Sher Shah reorganizes revenue, roads, currency and administration.

change.title: Mughal rule is interrupted
change.description: The Sur Empire demonstrates the continuing competition for control of northern India.

control.name: Mughal Empire
control.description: Akbar becomes emperor and begins a period of major territorial expansion and administrative consolidation.

response.title: Alliance as well as conquest
response.description: Akbar combines military expansion with alliances, particularly with several Rajput rulers.

change.title: Mughal power becomes more durable
change.description: A centralized imperial system develops that can govern a diverse population and territory.

control.name: Mughal Empire
control.description: Mughal authority expands across northern and central India and into Gujarat and Bengal.

response.title: Resistance, alliance and incorporation
response.description: Different communities and rulers respond through warfare, negotiation, alliance and incorporation into the imperial system.

change.title: Mughal territory expands across the subcontinent
change.description: The Mughal Empire becomes one of the dominant political powers in India.

control.name: Mughal Empire
control.description: Shah Jahan rules during a period of considerable Mughal wealth, territorial power and architectural activity.

response.title: Imperial culture expands
response.description: Court culture, architecture and administration become major expressions of imperial authority.

change.title: Imperial authority becomes highly visible
change.description: Monumental architecture becomes an important symbol of Mughal power.

control.name: Mughal Empire
control.description: Aurangzeb expands Mughal territory deep into the Deccan.

response.title: Resistance intensifies
response.description: Marathas, Sikhs and other regional powers challenge Mughal authority.

change.title: The empire reaches enormous scale
change.description: Mughal territorial expansion reaches its greatest extent, but governing the enlarged empire becomes increasingly difficult.

control.name: Maratha state
control.description: Shivaji is formally crowned and establishes an independent Maratha kingdom in western India.

response.title: Resistance becomes state-building
response.description: Opposition to Mughal and other regional powers develops into an organized Maratha state.

change.title: A new regional power emerges
change.description: Maratha political power becomes a major force in western and later central India.

control.name: Mughal Empire
control.description: Aurangzeb dies after a long reign marked by extensive expansion and prolonged warfare.

response.title: Regional powers assert themselves
response.description: Marathas, Sikhs, Rajputs and other regional powers increasingly challenge Mughal authority.

change.title: Central authority weakens
change.description: The Mughal Empire remains important but loses effective control over increasing parts of the subcontinent.

control.name: Mughal and regional authorities
control.description: Mughal authority remains significant in northern India while Sikh communities develop stronger collective organization.

response.title: Collective resistance
response.description: Guru Gobind Singh establishes the Khalsa, strengthening Sikh military and communal organization.

change.title: A new political force develops
change.description: Sikh communities become increasingly organized as a political and military force.

control.name: Maratha Confederacy
control.description: Maratha power expands rapidly across central and northern India as Mughal authority weakens.

response.title: Regional states negotiate and resist
response.description: Local rulers respond to Maratha expansion through alliances, tribute, resistance and political negotiation.

change.title: The political map changes again
change.description: The Marathas become one of the most powerful political forces in eighteenth-century India.

eras.title: Battle of Plassey
eras.subtitle: The East India Company gains political power

control.name: East India Company
control.description: The Company's victory over the Nawab of Bengal gives it decisive political influence in Bengal.

response.title: Opposition to Company power
response.description: Political and military opposition continues as the Company expands its influence.

change.title: A trading company becomes a political power
change.description: The East India Company begins transforming its commercial influence into territorial authority.

control.name: East India Company
control.description: Company forces defeat the combined armies of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.

response.title: Regional rulers challenge Company expansion
response.description: Indian rulers attempt to prevent the Company from becoming the dominant political force in eastern India.

change.title: Company control deepens
change.description: The victory strengthens the Company's political and fiscal position in Bengal and Bihar.

eras.title: Mysore Resists
eras.subtitle: A major challenge to Company expansion

control.name: Kingdom of Mysore
control.description: Mysore develops into a powerful state that repeatedly challenges British expansion in southern India.

response.title: Organized military resistance
response.description: Haider Ali and Tipu Sultan build military power and fight several wars against the Company and its allies.

change.title: The Company faces organized opposition
change.description: Mysore becomes one of the most significant obstacles to British expansion in southern India.

control.name: East India Company
control.description: The defeat of the Maratha Confederacy removes the last major Indian power capable of challenging Company supremacy across much of the subcontinent.

response.title: Resistance continues locally
response.description: Although Maratha political dominance ends, opposition to Company rule continues in many regions.

change.title: Company power becomes dominant
change.description: The political balance shifts decisively toward British-controlled territories and allied princely states.

eras.title: Revolt of 1857
eras.subtitle: The Company faces a major uprising

control.name: East India Company
control.description: Company rule faces a major uprising involving soldiers, rulers and civilians across parts of northern and central India.

response.title: Widespread armed resistance
response.description: The uprising spreads through several major centers, with different groups joining for different political and social reasons.

change.title: Company rule collapses
change.description: The revolt fails militarily but fundamentally changes the structure of British rule in India.

control.name: British Crown
control.description: The Government of India Act 1858 transfers governance from the East India Company to the British Crown.

response.title: Political organization changes
response.description: Indian political responses increasingly move toward education, associations, petitions, reform movements and eventually organized nationalism.

change.title: Company rule becomes Crown rule
change.description: India is governed directly on behalf of the British Crown.

control.name: British Raj
control.description: British colonial authority remains firmly established.

response.title: Political organization
response.description: Indian political leaders establish the Indian National Congress to create a platform for political discussion and representation.

change.title: Indian nationalism becomes organized
change.description: A nationwide political organization begins developing within colonial India.

eras.title: Partition of Bengal
eras.subtitle: A new wave of political resistance

control.name: British Raj
control.description: The British government partitions Bengal, officially citing administrative reasons.

response.title: Swadeshi movement
response.description: Large protests, boycotts and promotion of Indian-made goods develop in response to the partition.

change.title: Mass political participation grows
change.description: Anti-colonial politics expands beyond elite political organizations into broader public movements.

control.name: British Raj
control.description: British troops under General Dyer fire on a gathering in Amritsar.

response.title: Public outrage
response.description: The massacre generates widespread outrage and strengthens opposition to colonial rule.

change.title: Trust in colonial rule collapses further
change.description: The event becomes a major catalyst for India's independence movement.

control.name: British Raj
control.description: British colonial institutions continue to govern India.

response.title: Mass non-cooperation
response.description: Gandhi and the Indian National Congress encourage people to withdraw cooperation from selected colonial institutions.

change.title: The independence movement becomes mass politics
change.description: Large numbers of Indians participate in organized anti-colonial politics.

control.name: British Raj
control.description: The British government maintains laws controlling the production and taxation of salt.

response.title: Civil disobedience
response.description: Gandhi leads a march to the coast to challenge the colonial salt laws, helping launch a wider civil disobedience movement.

change.title: Colonial laws are challenged through mass action
change.description: Civil disobedience becomes a central method of the independence movement.

control.name: British Raj
control.description: Britain retains ultimate authority while introducing expanded provincial autonomy and electoral representation.

response.title: Political participation
response.description: Indian political parties increasingly participate in provincial elections and governments.

change.title: Provincial politics expands
change.description: Indian politicians gain greater experience in operating elected governments.

control.name: British Raj
control.description: Britain continues to control India during the Second World War.

response.title: Quit India
response.description: The Indian National Congress launches a mass movement demanding an end to British rule.

change.title: The demand for independence becomes unavoidable
change.description: Although the movement is suppressed, British authority faces increasingly organized opposition.

control.name: Independent India
control.description: British rule ends and India becomes an independent country. Partition creates India and Pakistan.

response.title: Independence, celebration and displacement
response.description: Independence is accompanied by mass migration, communal violence and enormous social upheaval caused by Partition.

change.title: Colonial rule ends
change.description: Political sovereignty passes from the British Raj to independent governments.

control.name: Republic of India
control.description: India becomes a sovereign democratic republic under its new Constitution.

response.title: Citizens become constitutional participants
response.description: The Constitution establishes universal adult suffrage and a democratic political system.

change.title: India becomes a republic
change.description: Political authority is defined through a democratic Constitution rather than monarchy or colonial rule.

control.name: Elected government
control.description: India holds its first general election under universal adult suffrage.

response.title: Mass democratic participation
response.description: Millions of citizens participate in India's first national election.

change.title: Democracy becomes practical reality
change.description: India demonstrates that representative government can operate across an enormous and diverse population.

control.name: Republic of India
control.description: India reorganizes many state boundaries, largely around linguistic identities.

response.title: Language-based movements
response.description: Political movements and protests help push the government toward reorganizing states along linguistic lines.

change.title: The internal political map changes
change.description: India's federal structure is reshaped to better reflect linguistic and regional identities.

control.name: Republic of India
control.description: Government agricultural policies promote high-yield crops, irrigation, fertilizers and modern farming methods.

response.title: Farmers adopt new methods
response.description: Farmers in several regions adopt new technologies, dramatically increasing agricultural production.

change.title: India's food system changes
change.description: Agricultural productivity rises significantly, particularly in northwestern India.

control.name: India / Pakistan / Bangladesh
control.description: The conflict in East Pakistan develops into a war involving India and results in the creation of Bangladesh.

response.title: Mass displacement and political mobilization
response.description: Millions of people are displaced during the conflict, while the Bengali independence movement seeks a separate state.

change.title: The map of South Asia changes
change.description: Bangladesh becomes an independent country and India's eastern geopolitical environment is transformed.

control.name: Government of India
control.description: A national Emergency is declared, during which civil liberties and political opposition are heavily restricted.

response.title: Opposition and political resistance
response.description: Opposition leaders, activists and organizations challenge the government, and the Emergency eventually ends with elections.

change.title: The limits of political power are tested
change.description: The period becomes a major episode in India's democratic history.

control.name: Government of India
control.description: The government introduces major economic reforms reducing restrictions and opening the economy to greater global participation.

response.title: Economic transformation
response.description: Businesses, workers and consumers adapt to a more open and increasingly globalized economy.

change.title: The economic system shifts
change.description: Liberalization changes India's relationship with trade, investment and the global economy.

control.name: Republic of India
control.description: Government, private companies and citizens participate in rapid expansion of telecommunications and digital infrastructure.

response.title: Society goes digital
response.description: Mobile phones, internet access and digital services transform communication, commerce and everyday life.

change.title: Political and economic participation becomes increasingly digital
change.description: Technology creates new ways for citizens, businesses and governments to interact.

eras.title: Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization
eras.subtitle: A major constitutional and territorial change

control.name: Government of India
control.description: The constitutional status of Jammu and Kashmir is changed and the former state is reorganized into two union territories.

response.title: Political disagreement
response.description: The change produces significant political debate and differing responses within Jammu and Kashmir and across India.

change.title: The internal administrative map changes
change.description: The former state is reorganized as the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.

eras.title: Chandrayaan-3
eras.subtitle: India reaches the lunar south polar region

control.name: Republic of India
control.description: India's space program successfully lands Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon's south polar region.

response.title: National scientific achievement
response.description: The mission becomes a major symbol of India's scientific and technological capabilities.

change.title: India's technological influence grows
change.description: The achievement strengthens India's position as a major spacefaring nation.

control.name: Republic of India
control.description: India is a federal democratic republic in which political authority is exercised through constitutional institutions, elected governments and state governments.

response.title: Citizens shape political power
response.description: Citizens participate through elections, political parties, civil society, protests, media and democratic institutions.

change.title: From empires to constitutional democracy
change.description: Political authority in India has moved through kingdoms, empires, colonial rule and finally a democratic republic.
